worst_places.before: Margin collapsing merges adjacent vertical margins into a single margin equal to the larger of the two (not their sum). Three scenarios trigger it: (1) adjacent block siblings — the bottom margin of the first and top margin of the second collapse; (2) parent and first/last child — if no border, padding, or BFC separates them, the child's margin "leaks" out of the parent; (3) empty blocks — an element with no height, border, or padding collapses its own top and bottom margins.
worst_places.after:
Margin collapsing merges two adjacent vertical margins into one. The result is the larger of the two, not their sum.

Three cases trigger it:

1. **Adjacent block siblings.** The bottom margin of the first and the top margin of the second collapse into one.
2. **Parent and first or last child.** If nothing separates them — no border, no padding, no block formatting context (BFC) — the child's margin "leaks" out through the parent.
3. **Empty blocks.** An element with no height, no border and no padding collapses its own top and bottom margins together.

worst_places.after:
### Собственное соотношение сторон изображений

У каждого изображения есть собственное соотношение сторон — оно берётся из размеров исходного файла. `aspect-ratio` позволяет заранее занять под изображение место нужной формы, ещё до его загрузки, — тогда раскладка не дёрнется, когда картинка подгрузится:

patterns: The Russian version is the harder one, not the easier one — reversing the usual assumption. RU wins on syntax (B 4.4 vs 3.9, because Russian sentences here are genuinely shorter) but loses on terminology (A 2.8 vs 3.0, G 3.0) because the translation pass systematically drops the clarifying material the English carries: TTI's gloss (ru/09:265 vs en/09:265), CLS's gloss (ru/07:444 vs en/07:446), the written-out "assistive technologies" that makes AT guessable (ru/11:209 vs en/11:209), the clamp() formula line (ru/07:297), the IE/Edge caveat on focusable="false" (ru/01:154), the YAML remark (ru/09:390), and — worst — the entire six-example "Common accessibility mistakes" section of the site's only a11y article (ru/01, 15 headings vs 22, 24 fences vs 36). Any fix pass must diff ru against en per file, not read each locale on its own.

Russian articles code-switch where they should translate, in two distinct forms. (a) Multi-word English spec terms are left in Latin script mid-sentence — "Также создаёт: stacking context, block formatting context, containing block" (ru/08:233, repeated 239, 382; ru/11:229) — even though this same site translates all three elsewhere ("контекст наложения" ru/05, "контекст блочного форматирования" ru/02). (b) English words get Russian morphology bolted on to make non-words: "непромоутированных" (ru/11:163), "авторинг" (ru/09:485,503), "интринсическое/интринсическая/интринсический" (ru/07:433,435; ru/04:244; ru/11:39), "флюидный" (ru/07:261,291), "bucket-ы" (ru/06:447; ru/11:111), "drawer-ы" (ru/08:200; ru/11:25), "стилизованные" for "layered" (ru/06:210,453; ru/11:111 — this one destroys the sentence's meaning). Rule for the style guide: if the term has an established Russian form, use it and put the English in parentheses once; never inflect an English stem.

Abbreviations are introduced by a file the reader may not have opened, or by a section that comes later in the same file. BFC is used in en/02:118 and ru/02:118 but only defined at line 146 of the same file; in file 11 BFC's first use (line 13) is one question before its definition (line 17). ARIA is expanded only in 01, yet used 5x in 11. GPU (22x in 08, 7x in 11), CSSOM, CPU, DOM and VRAM are treated as shared vocabulary across 08 and 11. Because these files are read out of order and 11 is the natural entry point for interview prep, 11 is the file where the abbreviation debt lands hardest (A=1 in both locales).

File 11 inverts the zone's own best habit. The zone's outstanding strength is the answer-first lead — C scores 5 in all 22 files, and 11 is the purest example ("346px." / "No — one fraction of the available free space" / "Only transform and opacity."). But 11 pairs that with the zone's worst structure: 3,769 EN / 3,073 RU words, 33 over-long paragraphs, 36 EN sentences over 25 words, and zero code fences, tables or diagrams in either locale — in a file whose every answer is about code. The other ten articles average one code fence per ~85 words. The fix is not to cut answers but to let each answer show the two lines of CSS it is describing.

Two authoring self-corrections survived into published English prose, both in en/05 (line 128 "... wait, actually ..." and the Fix 2 block at 309-317 that retracts its own fix). Both are absent from ru/05, which means the Russian pass caught what the English pass did not — so English files need the same second read the Russian ones evidently got. Related smaller slips of the same kind: en/02:219 has a stray `**` closing a bold heading, en/03:227 says "use `margin-auto`" for `margin: auto`, en/06:74 and en/09:74 both read "Overriding is trivially:", ru/03:3 has "два оси" for "две оси", ru/11:215 has "объходить" for "обходить", and en/04:386 vs ru/04:386 disagree on `data-weekday="1"` vs `"2"` under an identical "Tuesday" comment.
notes: Zone-specific verdict on 01, the site's only real a11y article: a reader with no ARIA/WCAG/screen-reader vocabulary CAN follow the EN version, with four stumbles — "screen reader" and "announce" are used from line 19 as if known, "landmarks" arrives undefined at line 37, WCAG appears once at line 326 never expanded, and "input modality" carries the whole :focus-visible answer at line 454 while being the most opaque phrase in the file. Everything else is well built: ARIA is expanded on first use, the accessibility tree is explained before it is used, and the div-vs-button table is the best scaffolding in the zone. The RU version is materially worse for that reader: same four gaps plus "ориентиры" (a literal calque of landmarks with no currency in Russian a11y writing), bare "AT" (unguessable, since the RU expansion is "вспомогательные технологии"), "disclosure-виджетов" and "модальность ввода" — and it is missing the six-mistake practical section entirely. Recommended minimum: a four-line glossary paragraph after the H1 (screen reader, accessibility tree, landmark, WCAG) in both locales, plus restoring the missing RU section. Mechanical density (11.8 flags/1k) does understate this zone's problems only in files 05, 08 and 11; files 02, 03, 04 and 10 are genuinely ship-ready and 03 is the best-written article in the zone in both locales.
